brief: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% on 17 Sep, tightening policy just as S&P 500 breadth was already weakening beneath a headline index near record highs and above its 200-day moving average. About 32% of constituents are at least 20% below their peaks, well below the 52.8%-92.9% range hit in five prior stress episodes from 2016-2025, so damage is broad but not capitulation-level. The advance-decline line has fallen sharply from its July peak to about 1,462. Bear-market participation is worst in Technology (56.2%), Consumer Discretionary (51.1%), Industrials (43.4%) and Communication Services (37.5%), all above the 32.2% index average, while defensives Real Estate, Energy, Financials and Utilities sit at 13.3%-16.1%. The PTS Market Environment Indicator fell below its 5-point warning threshold, with only 3 of 8 bullish conditions met, historically preceding lower returns but much lower volatility and drawdown. As long as earnings growth holds up, the note reads this as rotation not liquidation, but warns that if weakness spreads to the largest-cap leaders, the correction could hit the benchmark directly. 7,492 is the key S&P support: holding it preserves a path toward 7,938-8,022 and 8,218, while a break exposes 7,314 and the 200-day SMA near 7,175.
